SAP Service Cloud Version 2 — Embedded Intelligence for Smarter Customer Interactions 
 In Part 1, we explored how SAP Cloud ERP uses AI to automate order creation, score financial risk, and monitor fulfillment in real time. Part 2 focuses on the service side of the Order-to-Cash stage — where the quality and speed of every customer interaction directly affects satisfaction and retention. 
 SAP Service Cloud Version 2, powered by the SAP CX AI Toolkit, embeds three AI capabilities directly into service professionals' daily workflows: Intelligent Customer Profile , Intelligent Q&A , and Record Summarization . Together, they eliminate manual data searches, surface relevant information instantly, and enable faster, more informed decisions. 
 Intelligent Customer Profile 
 When a service agent receives a customer email, they need context — fast. Searching through case histories and switching between systems before responding is time-consuming and error-prone. The Intelligent Customer Profile eliminates this entirely. 
 As soon as a customer email arrives, the Smart Actions dashboard automatically surfaces an AI-synthesized snapshot of that customer, built from data configured by your administrator. The profile is structured into five components: 
 Profile Header : The customer's name, image, and one administrator-configured highlighted attribute — such as service tier or case status — giving the agent the most critical piece of context at a glance 
 Highlighted Values : Up to three additional key data points, intentionally limited to prevent information overload at the moment of contact 
 Summary : An AI-generated narrative overview of the customer, dynamically produced from live data at the time of engagement — reflecting current status including recent cases, open opportunities, and updated account details 
 Details : The complete list of customer attributes from the configured data source, available when an agent needs to go deeper than the summary 
 Segments : Customer classifications based on shared characteristics or behaviors — such as demographics or purchasing activity. Knowing that a customer belongs to a segment like "high-value at-risk" can meaningfully change how an agent prioritizes and approaches the interaction 
 Segments are available when SAP Customer Data Platform is the data source. 
 Intelligent Q&A — Enterprise Knowledge, Instantly Searchable 
 Service agents regularly need answers from across the organization — past case resolutions, product specifications, internal process documents. Finding that information manually means switching between systems, searching knowledge bases, and reviewing case histories one by one. 
 Intelligent Q&A allows service professionals to ask natural language questions and receive precise, AI-generated answers grounded in real enterprise data. An agent can ask "How was a similar network connectivity issue resolved last quarter?" and receive a relevant, sourced answer in seconds. 
 Answers are retrieved from multiple connected sources: 
 Service cases and sales opportunities in SAP Sales Cloud and SAP Service Cloud Version 2 — covering the 1,000 most recently updated cases from day one, providing an immediate historical foundation 
 Documents in OneDrive, SharePoint, and Azure Blob Storage — internal guides, product manuals, and process documents (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .csv, .txt) up to 100 MB per file 
 Microsoft 365 meeting transcripts — key decisions and commitments from customer meetings, without manually reviewing recordings 
 SAP Commerce Cloud product specifications — compatibility details and technical specifications surfaced instantly for product-related queries 
 The result: your organization's institutional knowledge becomes directly searchable through natural language, without agents ever leaving the toolkit. 
 Record Summarization — Case Narratives Generated in Seconds 
 Managing high volumes of cases means agents constantly need to orient themselves on new records — reading through notes, email threads, and update histories before they can engage meaningfully with a customer or hand off a case. Record Summarization eliminates this effort. 
 A summarization triggered within the toolkit generates a coherent, natural-language narrative of a case, account, or opportunity — covering key events, current status, and relevant context — in seconds. This capability is particularly valuable at two specific points in the Order-to-Cash process: 
 Before a customer interaction : An agent instantly orients themselves on a case or account without manually reviewing the record history 
 During a case handoff : The receiving agent gets a clear, complete picture of what has happened and what still needs to be resolved, reducing the risk of context loss during transitions 

 The Bigger Picture — Parts 1 & 2 
 Across both parts of this series, a consistent pattern emerges: AI in the Order-to-Cash stage is not about replacing human judgment — it is about removing the manual effort that prevents humans from exercising it effectively. 
 SAP Cloud ERP ensures orders are created accurately, risks are identified early, and fulfillment issues are resolved before they affect customers. SAP Service Cloud Version 2 ensures that when customers do need to interact with the service team, every agent has the context, knowledge, and tools to respond immediately and accurately. 
 What makes this layer particularly powerful is its adaptability. Each AI capability continuously learns from user interactions and evolving data — becoming more accurate with every engagement, and delivering compounding operational value over time.

items.title: Who paid this? Applying cash with confidence in SAP
items.author: JyotiNarang
items.text:
Every company that collects through lockbox, ACH and wire has a residue of receipts that SAP cannot apply on its own. The cash is in the bank, but receivables don't yet know whose it is or which invoices it settles. That residue overstates DSO, puts paying customers on credit hold, weakens the cash forecast and leaves suspense balances for the close. 

 The cause is rarely missing information. It is information split across three streams that arrive at different times: the bank statement, the lockbox file and the customer's remittance advice. SAP imports the first two. The third arrives by EDI, email or a supplier portal and has no standard import. 
 This paper describes an agent that joins the three streams, scores who paid and what for separately, and acts only when both scores are high. When they aren't, it posts on account, suggests a match for one-click approval, or hands the item to an analyst with the evidence attached. It never changes master data, never writes off a customer deduction, and never posts through anything but SAP's own clearing logic. What the CFO gets 
 Working capital: cash applied the day it arrives, so DSO and the aged receivables report reflect what customers have actually paid. 
 Forecast quality: treasury sees receipts by customer, not as unidentified deposits. 
 Control: every decision stores its evidence and the rule that fired, which gives audit a complete trail. 
 Fraud resistance: spoofed remittances and requests to redirect refunds are stopped, not processed. 
 No lock-in: standard SAP keeps running underneath, and licensed products can feed the agent as one more signal. 
 The business problem 
 Why unapplied cash is a CFO problem, not an AR problem 
 DSO looks worse than it is 
 Paid invoices stay open until the cash is applied. Collections chase customers who have already paid, and the receivables ledger overstates risk. 
 Good customers get blocked 
 Credit management sees open items and blocks orders. Sales escalates, and the relationship pays for a back-office delay. 
 The forecast loses detail 
 Treasury knows the deposit total but not which customers paid. Customer-level payment behaviour, the input to a good cash forecast, arrives late. 
 Suspense balances reach the close 
 Unidentified receipts, lockbox clearing differences and on-account balances need explaining at month end, and auditors ask about them. Worked example (illustrative) 
 A company with USD 2 billion of annual credit sales collects about USD 5.5 million per day. Each day by which application lags, and each day of DSO, therefore ties up about USD 5.5 million of working capital in receivables reporting. Substitute your own figures; the arithmetic is the point, not the numbers. 
 Root cause 
 Three streams, and SAP imports only two Stream Format and SAP import What it carries, and what it loses 
 Bank statement BAI2 or camt.053 via FF_5 One line per credit. A lockbox line shows only the deposit total; ACH shows originator and trace; wires show free text or, with ISO 20022, structured data that a BAI2 file truncates. 
 Lockbox file BAI lockbox via FLB2 One record per check: amount, MICR bank details, a payer name cut to 34 characters, and invoice numbers keyed from the stub, sometimes wrongly. 
 Remittance advice EDI 820, email, PDF, portal. No standard import. The invoice list, deductions and reasons. Often arrives days after the cash, from a payer name that differs from the customer master. 
 Standard SAP identifies a customer through MICR bank details in KNBK or a valid invoice reference. The test pack behind this paper documents sixteen ways that breaks, from a new bank account or a parent paying for its subsidiaries to deductions, foreign-currency wires, missing stubs, bank file breaks and spoofed remittances. 
 The solution 
 Where the agent sits in the SAP landscape 

 Standard import stays untouched. The agent works only on what it could not clear, plus the remittances SAP never sees, and writes back through SAP's own processes. 
 This is a side-by-side extension, in line with a clean-core approach: no modification of standard lockbox or bank statement programs. The agent reads open and cleared items, customer master and bank details, the corporate group ( KONZS ) and payer partners ( KNVP ), an alias table and payment history. It writes only through standard postings and clearing, dispute management and master-data change requests. 
 The design 
 Two questions, four outcomes 
 The agent scores two things separately: how sure it is who paid , and how sure it is what the payment is for . Standard lockbox has two outcomes, cleared or not. The agent has four. Who paid What for Outcome Meaning 
 ≥ 0.97 ≥ 0.95 Auto-post Post and clear with no human touch. 
 ≥ 0.97 < 0.95 On account The cash sits on the right customer while the remittance is awaited. 
 0.80 – 0.97 any Suggest A prepared posting for one-click approval. 
 < 0.80, or a tie any Exception Research by an analyst, with the evidence attached. 
 If the two best candidate customers score within 0.15 of each other, the agent never auto-posts. The thresholds are starting values. A nightly replay against analyst decisions recommends changes, so that 0.97 means about 97 percent correct; the AR lead approves them within bands that finance controls set. 
 How the evidence is weighed 
 Every signal adds weighted evidence to the same two scores and records what it found. Cheap lookups run first only to save cost; a weak early signal never blocks a strong later one. 
 Hard keys: invoice numbers found in open items, MICR or debtor account in KNBK , ACH originator ID. 
 Remittance join: a bank or check reference matched to an 820, email, portal line or ISO 20022 structured remittance. 
 Remittance checksum: invoice lines less discounts and deductions must equal the payment. If they don't, a line was lost and the item cannot auto-post. 
 Sender trust: email remittances count only from registered domains. Lookalike domains are excluded and flagged. 
 Names and hierarchy: fuzzy matching against names and approved aliases, then corporate group and payer partners. 
 Learned signals: payment history and, where licensed, SAP Cash Application or SAP agent proposals. They add confidence but never decide alone. 
 Amount: used last. Amount alone never auto-posts. 
 A language model is used to read unstructured remittances and to explain decisions to analysts. It is never the only evidence for a posting. 
 Evidence 
 What the test pack shows 
 The design was worked through against 21 scenarios of synthetic BAI2, lockbox, EDI 820, ISO 20022 camt.054, email and portal files with matching SAP extracts. Eleven auto-post, five are suggested, two go on account and three become exceptions. Four cases show the judgement involved. 
 The amount trap 
 A partial payment's remainder equals a different open invoice. Amount-only matching would clear the wrong item; the agent follows the remittance and posts a partial payment. 
 The exchange-rate gap 
 USD 24,480.00 settles a CAD 34,000.00 invoice at the bank's rate of 0.7200. At SAP's 0.7230 the item is worth USD 24,582.00. The customer is certain; the 102.00 difference needs approval, so it is suggested. 
 The spoofed remittance 
 A real ACH payment is followed by an email from a lookalike domain asking for refunds to go to a new account. The email is excluded, the request goes to security review, and the cash is applied from bank data alone. 
 The broken file 
 The bank's lockbox deposit is 2,875.00 more than its detail file. The agent processes the checks it has, holds the gap in clearing and drafts the bank inquiry, instead of forcing the deposit to balance. 
 Governance 
 Controls a CFO can sign off Control Risk it addresses Evidence for audit 
 No master-data writes; new bank details become MDG change requests Fraudulent bank-detail changes Change request with approver 
 Bank-detail and refund requests go to security review Payment redirection, business email compromise Security case linked to the receipt 
 Remittances only from registered senders Spoofed remittances Sender check result per document 
 Remittance must add up to the payment Lost or misread lines Checksum result and gap amount 
 Amount alone never auto-posts; ties never auto-post Cash applied to the wrong invoice or customer Scores and rule fired 
 Deductions become dispute cases, never write-offs Margin leakage UDM case with reason code 
 Deposit must reconcile to its detail file Missing or extra items Reconciliation break record 
 Thresholds change only with approval, within set bands Silent loosening of controls Replay report and approval 
 Value caps per payment and per day Large single errors Cap breaches routed to Suggest 
 Segregation of duties is explicit: the agent proposes and posts within policy; AR analysts approve suggestions; the AR lead approves aliases and threshold changes; finance controls set the bands and caps; treasury reviews bank-detail requests; the master-data team approves bank accounts; internal audit has read-only access to every evidence record. 
 What has changed 
 Why now: three shifts in 2025–2026 
 Payments carry better data 
 Fedwire moved to ISO 20022 in July 2025, and banks are adding camt.052/053/054 reporting next to BAI2. Some plan to move SWIFT statements to camt by 2027. Structured remittance can now reach SAP, but only if the import reads it. The agent reads camt.054 next to BAI2. 
 SAP is adding agents 
 SAP now lists receivables agents, including dispute resolution and, for contract accounting, payment matching. Where licensed, their proposals become signals inside the same controls rather than a second, separately governed matcher. 
 Remittance fraud is rising 
 Lookalike domains and requests to redirect refunds target the gap between AR and treasury. A cash application process that trusts any email is now a control weakness. 
 AI needs governance 
 Boards and auditors expect AI decisions to be explainable and bounded. Two scores, four outcomes, hard rules in code and a complete evidence record meet that expectation. 
 Options 
 Build, buy or combine SAP Cash Application Specialist product (e.g. HighRadius) Agent pattern in this paper 
 What it is SAP's machine-learning matching service A packaged order-to-cash platform A design you build on SAP 
 Decision logic Learned from history Rules plus machine learning, vendor-managed Visible, owned in-house, rules in code 
 Remittance capture Depends on edition and inputs Broad: email, EDI, portals, lockbox Adapters you choose; any can be a product 
 Best when You run S/4HANA and want SAP-native You want a full platform quickly You need bank- and customer-specific rules and tight control 
 These are not exclusive. The pattern is designed to take any of these products' proposals as one more signal, so a company can buy where it helps and keep the decision policy and controls in its own hands. Vendor capabilities above come from public material and have not been independently tested. 
 Getting started 
 A 180-day path from baseline to scale Days 0–30 Baseline 
 Measure hit rate, unapplied cash and its age, touches per item and days on account. Days 30–90 Shadow 
 The agent decides but posts nothing. Compare every decision with the analysts'. Days 90–150 Suggest 
 Analysts approve agent proposals with one click. Calibrate thresholds. Days 150–180 Auto-post 
 Turn on auto-post one customer segment at a time, inside the value caps. 
 What to report to the CFO Measure Why it matters 
 Unapplied and on-account cash, by age The working-capital number; it should fall and stay low. 
 Same-day application rate How much cash is applied on the day it arrives. 
 Auto-post reversal rate Quality. The design target is below 0.2 percent. 
 Analyst touches per receipt Capacity freed for disputes and collections. 
 Security reviews raised and confirmed Fraud attempts stopped before money moved. 
 What the SAP team provides 
 Lockbox control and posting data

items.title: SAP Analytics Cloud – Dynamic Chart and Table Visibility Using Radio Buttons
items.author: saikat_pal5
items.text:
Introduction 
 SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) enables developers to create interactive and user-friendly analytical stories that provide greater flexibility in presenting business information. In many dashboard scenarios, users may want to switch between a graphical chart view and a detailed tabular view without displaying both visualizations simultaneously. A Radio Button Group provides a simple and effective way to achieve this by allowing users to select their preferred visualization. Using the onSelect event, SAC scripting can dynamically control the visibility of the chart and table based on the selected option. When BarChart is selected, the chart is displayed while the table is hidden, and when FlatTable is selected, the table is displayed while the chart is hidden. . The functionality can be implemented using SAC scripting methods such as getSelectedKey() and setVisible() . This article explains the step-by-step configuration of the Radio Button Group and the scripting logic required to implement dynamic Chart and Table visibility in SAP Analytics Cloud .

items.title: Introducing the Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent
items.author: PatrickBao
items.text:
For accounts payable and receivable accountants, clearing open items is one of the most routine yet time-consuming tasks in the financial close process. While we already provides powerful automated clearing function — such as Clear Open Items Automatically (F.13) application and bank statement-driven automatic matching — a significant portion of open items still falls outside the reach of these automated processes. 
 The Challenge: The Gaps in Automated Clearing 
 In real-world business operations, especially for large enterprises processing thousands of transactions every week or month, common scenarios that resist automation include: 
 Missing or incomplete clearing references, preventing the system from establishing a match; 
 Remittances received after the actual payment date, causing timing mismatches between payment and invoice data; 
 Manual allocation of credit memos or down payments, requiring accountant judgment to resolve. 
 These leftover items accumulate quickly, placing a considerable burden on accounting teams. 
 The Solution: Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent 
 To improve these pain points, we introduce the Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent — an AI-powered agent designed to intelligently identify and match offsetting open items and automatically generate pre-validated clearing proposals for accountants to review and post. 
 At the heart of the agent is AI-driven fuzzy matching, applied across three commonly used reference fields — Assignment, Item Text, and Reference — enabling the agent to identify potential matches . 
 How It Works 
 The accountant trigger s the agent directly within Joule Chat, specifying a company code and optionally narrowing the scope to a specific customer or supplier. The agent runs in the background, checking identical or similar reference information across the relevant open items and generating proposals strictly for zero-balanced item combinations. Once ready, the agent notifies the user via in-system notification or email. 
 The accountant can then review the proposal, choosing to post or delete individual entries. 
 Upon acceptance, a clearing document is posted automatically and becomes visible in Manage Journal Entry or Display Journal Entry. 
 Prerequisites 
 Before you can start leveraging the Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent, there are a few things to have in place on both the platform and system configuration side. 
 Joule Integration 
 The agent runs within Joule, so the starting point is ensuring that Joule has been set up and successfully integrated with your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. If this integration is not yet in place, refer to the Integrating Joule with SAP Solutions documentation for guidance. 
 Note that access to this feature may require additional entitlements and authorizations — if you have questions about licensing or eligibility, reach out to your SAP account executive. 

 Scope Item Activation 
 On the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition side, two scope items need to be active in your system: 
 Accounts Receivable – J59 
 Accounts Payable – J60 

 User Authorizations 
 To review and act on clearing proposals, users must have the following IAM applications assigned to their business user : 
 Manage Customer Clearing Proposals (F9287) — for the receivables side 
 Manage Supplier Clearing Proposals (F9300) — for the payables side 
 These apps are delivered as part of the following business catalogs, which your system administrator can assign to the business roles: 
 SAP_SFIN_BC_AR_CLEARING — Accounts Receivable - Clearing 
 SAP_SFIN_BC_AP_CLEARING — Accounts Payable - Clearing 
 Once all of the above are confirmed, you are ready to put the agent to work. 
 How to Use 
 Getting started with the agent is straightforward. 
 Trigger the Agent in Joule Chat 
 Open the Joule chat window in your SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system. 
 Depending on your setup, Joule may first ask you to select the assistant you want to work with — choose either Financial Closing Assistant or Accounts Payable Assistant. 

 Once you are in the right context, simply send a message to kick things off. Something like: 
 "Clear open items for customer /supplier & in company code & " 

 Provide the Required Information 
 The agent will confirm what it needs before proceeding. T he agent asked to specify at least the company code to be processed. For example, I simply replied " Clear AR in company code 1010". 

 Once you supply the information, the agent acknowledges the input and gets to work. It will let you know that the clearing proposals are being generated in the background, and that you will receive a notification once the proposals are ready for your review. 

 Open the Notification and Navigate to the Proposal App 
 When the agent has finished processing, you will receive a notification — either via the in-system notification bell or by email. Click the notification to open it. 

 The notification confirms that AI-generated clearing proposals for the specified company code are ready for review. Click the link inside the notification and you will be taken directly to the relevant application: 
 If the agent was triggered for customer open items, it will open the Manage Customer Clearing Proposals (F9287) app. 
 If triggered for supplier open items, it will navigate to the Manage Supplier Clearing Proposals (F9300) app. 

 Review the Clearing Proposal Details 
 Inside the application, you will see the full list of proposed open item matches — in this example, 153 items are listed, organized into several clearing proposal groups. 

 Each group represents a set of items that the agent has identified as candidates for clearing against each other. For instance, the first group — Clearing Proposal 1 — contains two matched items. 
 To understand why the agent grouped these items together, click the Reasoning icon next to the group. This gives you a transparent view of the AI's matching logic, so you can make an informed decision on whether to accept the proposal. 

 Post or Delete the Proposal 
 Once you are satisfied with a clearing proposal group, select it and click Post. The agent will immediately generate the corresponding journal entry. 

 After posting, you have two options: 
 Navigate to Manage Journal Entries to view the full details of the posted document. 
 Return to the proposal list to continue reviewing and posting the remaining proposal groups. 

 If you are not happy with a particular proposal , you can simply delete it. The agent will not post anything . 
 *Image/data in this blog is from SAP internal systems, sample data, or demo systems. Any resemblance to real data is purely coincidental.* 
 Wrapping Up 
 The Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent represents a meaningful step forward in how finance teams handle one of their most persistent day-to-day challenges. By bringing AI-powered matching into the clearing workflow, it removes much of the manual effort . Every proposal is transparent and reviewable before anything is posted. 
 Whether you are dealing with high transaction volumes, recurring reconciliation bottlenecks, or simply looking to accelerate your month-end close, this agent is worth exploring. 
 For detailed information , visit the SAP Help Portal .

items.title: How AI Powers the Lead-to-Opportunity Stage in SAP Sales Cloud Version 2
items.author: Parisa_Mahdavi
items.text:
Sales professionals spend a significant portion of their time on activities that AI can now handle better and faster — deciding which leads to call first, researching accounts before a meeting, gauging whether a deal is at risk, and preparing talking points tailored to a specific customer. SAP Sales Cloud Version 2 embeds AI capabilities directly into the sales workflow to address exactly these challenges, helping sellers prioritize more precisely, understand customers more deeply, and walk into conversations better prepared. 
 This post walks through each AI capability available in the Lead-to-Opportunity stage and explains what it does, how it works, and where it delivers value. 
 Base AI vs. Premium AI: Understanding the Two Tiers 
 SAP Sales Cloud Version 2 distinguishes between two categories of AI capability: 
 Base AI — delivered out-of-the-box with the standard license at no additional cost. Includes Lead & Opportunity Scoring, Sentiment Analysis, and Relationship Intelligence. 
 Premium AI — requires AI Units for activation. Includes Account Synopsis and Lead Booster. 
 This distinction matters when planning adoption: Base AI capabilities are available immediately, while Premium AI requires license planning but unlocks generative AI features that go significantly further in depth. 
 Lead & Opportunity Scoring — Prioritize the Pipeline With Predictive Intelligence 
 Not all leads deserve equal attention. The challenge has always been knowing which ones to focus on. Lead & Opportunity Scoring answers that question using machine learning. 
 How Lead Intelligence Works 
 The Lead Intelligence model is trained on your organization's historical lead data — specifically leads that were converted into opportunities and leads that were declined. From these patterns, the system builds a customer-specific predictive model and applies it to score all open leads. 
 Scores range from 0 to 99 and are grouped into three color-coded bands: 
 0–50 : Less likely to convert 
 51–75 : Likely to convert 
 76–99 : Very likely to convert 
 For accurate scoring, the model requires a minimum of 1,000 converted and 1,000 declined leads , at least 12 months of lead lifecycle data , and sufficient data volume in any custom fields added to the scoring scenario. 
 Key Factors — Transparency Behind the Score 
 When a sales representative opens a scored lead, the Insight section displays up to six factors that most influenced the score, split across two types: 
 Dynamic Key Factors : Adaptive factors whose influence changes over time, such as Activity Count, Qualification Level, and Last Interaction — categorized as highly influencing (green) or minimally influencing (red). 
 Static Key Factors : Non-changing attributes such as Account Industry, Lead Source, and Lead Priority. 
 This transparency is important: sellers can see not just the score, but why a lead received that score and what signals are driving the prediction. 
 How Deal Intelligence Works 
 Deal Intelligence applies the same principle to opportunities. The model is trained on historical won and lost opportunities and assigns a win probability to each open deal — enabling sales representatives to prioritize their pipeline based on data-driven probabilities rather than intuition alone. 
 Scores are dynamic , refreshing daily around midnight in the data center's timezone using the latest customer data, interactions, and KPIs. Administrators configure both models under System Settings → AI Configuration → Narrow AI, with a Readiness Report verifying whether sufficient historical data exists before model training begins. 
 Sentiment & Relationship Intelligence — Reading the Room, Mapping the Network 
 Knowing a lead's score tells you where to focus. Understanding the emotional tone of your customer communications and the strength of your relationships tells you how to engage. 
 Sentiment Analysis 
 SAP Sales Cloud Version 2 uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) to analyze text from emails and surveys and determine whether the language is positive or negative — and how intense that sentiment is. 
 For sellers working through the Lead-to-Opportunity stage, this provides an automated emotional pulse of customer communications. Negative sentiment shifts can flag at-risk leads before they go cold. Positive sentiment can signal readiness to progress — prompting the right follow-up at the right time. 
 Relationship Intelligence and Hugrank 
 Relationship Intelligence automatically builds a smart network map of your organization's professional relationships. At the center of this is Hugrank — a quantitative measure of relationship strength scored from 0 to 100 , calculated based on approximately one year of communication history including email recency, frequency, reply rates, and calendar events. 
 Hugrank is grouped into three bands: 
 70–100 : Strong, active relationship 
 40–69 : Average, needs attention 
 0–39 : Poor engagement, at risk 
 Hugrank scores are accessible from the Relationship Intelligence facets within account and contact records and from the "My Network" workcenter in SAP Sales Cloud and SAP Service Cloud Version 2. 
 The business value in the Lead-to-Opportunity stage is direct: sellers can identify warm connections within an account, leverage internal colleagues who already have strong relationships with key stakeholders, and navigate deal cycles more effectively by understanding who knows who and how strong those relationships are. 
 Account Synopsis — Walk Into Every Conversation Prepared 
 First impressions in sales conversations are hard to recover from. Walking into a meeting without knowledge of an account's business challenges, competitive landscape, or strategic priorities is a missed opportunity — and manual research takes time that most sellers do not have. 
 Account Synopsis is a generative AI feature that produces a comprehensive, AI-generated summary of a customer account across multiple configurable dimensions, including: 
 Business Overview 
 Competitive Landscape 
 Business Challenges 
 Business Strategies 
 The synopsis is generated dynamically , reflecting the current market situation rather than relying solely on manually entered CRM data. Administrators activate it under System Settings → Generative AI Settings, choosing which sections to display for their organization. 
 In the Lead-to-Opportunity stage, Account Synopsis delivers value by: 
 Enabling sales representatives to walk into first conversations with deep account knowledge, addressing specific pain points and demonstrating industry awareness 
 Accelerating account planning by providing structured intelligence without manual research 
 Supporting lead qualification by helping sales reps assess whether the account's needs and strategies align with the products being offered 
 Facilitating more personalized engagement that builds trust and increases conversion probability 
 Account Synopsis is a Premium AI capability requiring AI Units. 
 Lead Booster — From Knowing Which Lead to Knowing How to Approach It 
 Lead & Opportunity Scoring tells you which leads to prioritize. Lead Booster tells you how to approach them. 
 Lead Booster is a generative AI feature that provides customized, AI-generated selling intelligence for each individual lead. It generates tailored content across configurable themes, including: 
 Company Understanding 
 Industry Needs 
 Pain Points 
 Strategic Alignment 
 Product Benefits 
 Scalability, Customization, and Competitive Advantage 
 The content is generated based on the account context, the products associated with the lead record, and market intelligence — meaning the guidance is specific to that lead, not generic talking points. 
 Lead Scoring vs. Lead Booster — Two Capabilities, One Workflow 
 Aspect Lead Score Lead Booster 
 AI Type Predictive ML (supervised learning) Generative AI (LLM-based) 
 Purpose Prioritize which leads to pursue Guide on how to approach each lead 
 Output Numeric score (0–99) + key factors Structured text with selling themes 
 Training data Previously converted/declined leads Account context + market intelligence 
 License Base AI (included) Premium AI (requires AI Units) 
 Update frequency Daily batch scoring On-demand generation 
 The two capabilities are designed to work together: scoring identifies the opportunity, Lead Booster equips the seller to act on it. 
 In the Lead-to-Opportunity stage, Lead Booster delivers business value by: 
 Reducing time spent on lead research and conversation preparation by up to 90% 
 Helping new or less experienced sales representatives perform at the level of seasoned account managers by providing ready-to-use selling guidance 
 Increasing conversion rates directly by enabling more relevant and consultative initial conversations 
 Lead Booster is a Premium AI capability requiring AI Units. Products must be entered in the lead record for product-specific guidance to be generated. The feature is currently available on iOS mobile devices. 
 A Connected AI Layer Across the Sales Workflow 
 These capabilities are not isolated features — they form a connected layer of intelligence across the Lead-to-Opportunity stage: 
 Lead & Opportunity Scoring tells sellers where to focus their pipeline 
 Sentiment Analysis surfaces the emotional tone of ongoing communications 
 Relationship Intelligence maps the strength of stakeholder connections 
 Account Synopsis provides deep, structured account knowledge before the first conversation 
 Lead Booster delivers lead-specific selling guidance at the moment of engagement 
 Together, they address the core challenge of the Lead-to-Opportunity stage: helping sales professionals identify the right prospects, understand them deeply, and engage with the kind of relevance and preparation that turns leads into opportunities. 
 Lead & Opportunity Scoring and Sentiment & Relationship Intelligence are Base AI capabilities included in the standard SAP Sales Cloud Version 2 license. Account Synopsis and Lead Booster are Premium AI capabilities requiring AI Units for activation.

items.title: From Campaign Creation to Conversion: How AI Is Reshaping Marketing in SAP Engagement Cloud
items.author: Parisa_Mahdavi
items.text:
Marketing has always involved a degree of guesswork — which subject line will get opened, which product will resonate, which contact is ready to buy. AI is steadily replacing that guesswork with precision. SAP Engagement Cloud (SAP Emarsys) and SAP Customer Data Platform embed AI capabilities directly into the platforms where marketers already work — not as separate tools to switch between, but as integrated intelligence woven into campaign creation, delivery, reporting, and audience targeting. 
 Here is a practical walkthrough of what those capabilities are and what they actually do. 
 SAP Engagement Cloud: AI Built Into Every Stage of the Campaign 
 Subject Line Generator — Better First Impressions, Faster 
 The subject line is the single most important variable in email marketing. It determines whether an email gets opened or ignored — and writing good ones at scale is harder than it sounds. 
 The Subject Line Generator , built directly into the Visual Content Editor (VCE), solves this through a two-phase process. In the first phase, it scans the email body, extracts keywords, identifies the purpose and tone, and captures brand signals. In the second phase, it feeds that analysis to a large language model (LLM) to produce a configured number of subject line variants — ready to rate, use, or refine. 
 The result: marketers get multiple high-quality options in seconds instead of drafting variations manually. In a contact-to-lead context, a stronger subject line drives higher open rates, which means more contacts engage with content and move closer to conversion. 
 Preheader Generator — The Second Line of the First Impression 
 If the subject line gets the email opened, the preheader seals the deal. The short preview text that appears after the subject line in most email clients is frequently underused — written as an afterthought or left as a default placeholder. 
 The Preheader Generator treats the preheader as a strategic element. It analyzes both the subject line and the email content together and generates preheader variants that complement and extend the subject line's message — not just repeat it. 
 An Autogenerate Preheader checkbox takes this further: when enabled, the preheader is generated automatically without any additional manual steps, streamlining campaign creation for high-volume teams. 
 AI-Assisted Report Builder — Analytics Without the Technical Bottleneck 
 Understanding campaign performance has traditionally required either technical query skills or dependence on a small number of people who have them. Neither is efficient at scale. 
 The AI-Assisted Report Builder changes the dynamic by allowing marketers to ask plain-language questions and receive structured campaign reports in return — no technical skills required. Questions like: 
 "What was the revenue from SMS campaigns last month?" 
 "What are the monthly year-to-date and year-over-year comparisons for Open Rate, Click Rate, and Conversion Rate for my batch campaigns?" 
 The AI translates the question into a reporting schema — metrics, date range, grouping, filters, sorting — and generates a structured report with table visualizations. If a question cannot be fully answered, the tool surfaces alternative questions based on the original query. 
 For marketing teams, this means faster decisions and broader access to analytics across the organization, without creating a bottleneck on technical resources. 
 Send Time Optimization — Right Message, Right Person, Right Moment 
 Even the most compelling email fails if it arrives at the wrong time. Sending a campaign to your entire audience at a single fixed time ignores a simple reality: different people check their email at different times. 
 Send Time Optimization (STO) addresses this by analyzing each recipient's historical email engagement behavior and delivering the next email at the individually optimal time — not a single blast, but a staggered, personalized delivery across the audience. 
 The algorithm balances two behaviors: 
 Exploitation : Using existing historical data to send at times already known to perform well for a specific contact. 
 Exploration : When little historical data exists, experimenting with different send times to discover better engagement windows. 
 The more campaigns you run, the smarter STO becomes. For scheduled campaigns, sends are distributed from 00:00 through to 22:00 on the launch day. For manually launched campaigns, sends are staggered over 24 hours from when calculations complete. 
 The compounding effect matters: every additional campaign adds more behavioral data, making each subsequent send more precisely timed than the last. 
 SAP Engagement Cloud Predict — Real-Time Personalization at Scale 
 Personalization is one of the most frequently cited marketing priorities and one of the least frequently delivered at scale. Predict is SAP Engagement Cloud's machine learning-powered recommendation engine — and it is built specifically to close that gap. 
 Predict analyzes behavioral data collected from your web shop: page views, add-to-cart events, checkouts, and search queries. It uses that data to deliver personalized product recommendations across email, web, and mobile in real time. 
 A key architectural strength is the Unified Profile. Predict recognizes users across multiple channels and devices and combines their browsing behavior into a single profile. Anonymous profiles are matched with identified contacts as soon as an identification event occurs — such as clicking a tracked email link — ensuring maximum coverage across all touchpoints. 
 Email Recommendations 
 Predict powers three primary email use cases: 
 Abandoned Cart — Triggered 30 minutes after cart abandonment, showing remaining items and complementary AI recommendations 
 Post-Purchase — Triggered by a purchase event, recommending complementary or likely next purchases 
 Abandoned Browse — Triggered 20 minutes after browsing stops, delivering personalized recommendations based on browse history or best-sellers 
 Revenue attribution is tracked through a dedicated dashboard: web recommendation revenue is attributed when a customer clicks and purchases in the same session; email recommendation revenue is attributed when a contact purchases anything within seven days of clicking through. A/B testing is available across all delivery channels to validate the impact of Predict recommendations against existing approaches. 
 SAP Customer Data Platform: Predictive Intelligence for Smarter Targeting 
 While SAP Engagement Cloud focuses on how you communicate with contacts, SAP Customer Data Platform focuses on who to target, when , and why — applying machine learning directly to unified customer data to generate forward-looking predictions about behavior. 
 Predictive Indicators — Acting on What Customers Are Likely to Do Next 
 Not all contacts are equal. Predictive Indicators help you act on that reality by generating machine learning-powered scores from existing customer profile, group, and activity data. 
 Four core model types are available — each applicable to both individual Profiles and Groups: 
 Model What It Predicts 
 Propensity to Buy Which contacts are most likely to make a purchase 
 Churn Which contacts are at risk of disengaging 
 Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) Expected profit margin over a defined period 
 True Customer Lifetime Value (TCLV) CLV refined by subtracting product returns — more accurate for high-return industries 
 The practical implication is significant: rather than treating every contact the same, your team can prioritize high-propensity leads, re-engage at-risk contacts before they go cold, and allocate marketing investment where it will generate the greatest return. 
 AI Workbench — A Centralized Intelligence Hub 
 The AI Workbench is the advanced analytics and model management environment within SAP Customer Data Platform. It is designed for business analysts and data-science-oriented users who need more than standard dashboards — bringing predictive models, visual insights, and performance monitoring into a single workspace. 
 The workbench is organized around three pillars: 
 Dashboards bring multiple insights together into a single monitoring view — for example, combining Customer Lifetime Value Profiles, Churn Probability Distribution, and Churn Risk Over Time into one consolidated screen. 
 Insights provide ready-to-use visualizations to help teams interpret predictive results without creating custom reports: 
 Churn Insights : Show churn risk by segment and the distribution of churn probabilities 
 CLV Insights : Show average CLV, profile distribution, and CLV trends over time 
 All insights are parameterized by solution, predictive indicator, and run ID, and support time periods from days (up to 365) through to years. 
 Manage Models provides full configuration control over all eight model variants across the four core model types — Churn, CLV, Propensity to Buy, and TCLV — for both Profiles and Groups. This goes significantly deeper than the standard Predictive Indicators module, giving users the ability to configure model run parameters, review previous runs, and tune models to specific business contexts. 
 The Bigger Picture: Intelligence Across the Full Contact-to-Lead Journey 
 What makes this stack meaningful is how the capabilities connect. SAP Engagement Cloud ensures the right message is crafted, optimized, delivered at the right time, and personalized to individual behavior. SAP Customer Data Platform ensures the right contacts are targeted in the first place — with predictive scores that surface who is ready to buy, who is at risk of churning, and where lifetime value is concentrated. 
 Together, they shift marketing from a volume game to a precision one. Less guesswork, more signal. Less broadcast, more relevance. And the more data these systems accumulate, the sharper the intelligence becomes — creating a compounding advantage that improves with every campaign, every click, and every conversion.

 We are excited to announce the rollout of Multi-Dimensional Analysis (MDA) – a modern, Fiori-based analytical application designed to deliver powerful multi-dimensional data analysis capabilities with an enhanced user experience. 
 MDA represents the evolution of our analytical tools, offering a cloud-native, responsive alternative to the traditional Web Dynpro Data Grid (WDPG). Built on SAP Fiori design principles, MDA brings:

 Legacy UI technology : Web Dynpro is being phased out in favor of modern web technologies.

 Complex navigation : Multiple nested dialogs and menus can be overwhelming. 
 Cloud readiness : WDPG was designed for on-premise deployment patterns.

 User Experience : Intuitive side panels, cleaner dialogs, and contextual actions. 
 Cloud-native design : Designed specifically for cloud deployment and scale. 
 Future-proof investment : A foundation for ongoing enhancements and new analytical capabilities

 Frequently Asked Questions

items.title: End-User Principal Propagation to SAP SuccessFactors via API Management and Microsoft Entra ID
items.author: Mohammed-inf
items.text:
Introduction 
 When an app calls SAP SuccessFactors on behalf of an employee, it usually signs in with one shared technical user. SuccessFactors then can't tell who is really calling: everyone gets the technical user's permissions, and every change shows the technical user's name. 
 This post shows how to make the call run as the signed-in employee instead, so each person can see and change only what their own role-based permissions (RBP) allow. This is called principal propagation . The employee signs in with Microsoft Entra ID, API Management exchanges their token at SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (IAS), and SAP SuccessFactors runs the call as that employee. 
 SAP has published the machine-to-machine version of this pattern in Standardized OIDC API Access to SAP SuccessFactors via SAP API Management and Microsoft Entra ID . It uses the same JWT Bearer token exchange (RFC 7523) for a technical user. This post extends it to end users, and reading SAP's post first will help. 
 In scope: user-delegated API access from external applications (mobile, web or portal) through an API management layer. The pattern does not depend on one gateway product: any API management solution that can verify a JWT, call a token endpoint and set a header can implement it. 
 The Challenge: A Technical User for Every External Application 
 With a technical user, every external application holds an SAP SuccessFactors credential, and the same credential often ends up in middleware, test collections and scripts. Its permissions are usually far wider than any single employee's. 
 The goal is a design where: 
 The API consumer authenticates users only with the identity provider it already uses – Microsoft Entra ID. 
 No SAP credential is stored in the API consumer. 
 SAP SuccessFactors receives only IAS-issued access tokens, preserving SAP's trust model. 
 Each API call runs as the signed-in employee, so RBP, business rules and the audit trail apply to that person. 
 Solution Overview 
 API Management is the central brokering point. The inbound call carries the employee's Microsoft Entra ID token. The API proxy exchanges it for an IAS-issued access token through a token call to IAS, then forwards the IAS token to SAP SuccessFactors. 

 Component 
 Role in the pattern 

 Microsoft Entra ID 
 Signs the employee in and issues an ID token to the API consumer's app registration. 

 API consumer 
 The external application the employee uses. Sends the employee's ID token with each call. 

 API Management 
 Verifies the Entra ID token, performs the JWT Bearer Token Exchange at IAS, replaces the token and routes the call to SAP SuccessFactors. 

 SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (IAS) 
 Trusts Entra ID as a corporate identity provider, resolves the employee to an IAS user, and issues an access token for the SAP SuccessFactors application. 

 SAP SuccessFactors 
 Target API. Accepts IAS-issued tokens (SAP Note 3681224) and runs the call as the employee. 
 Architecture Diagram 

 Step-by-Step Authentication Flow 
 1. The employee signs in to the API consumer with Microsoft Entra ID. The API consumer uses the Authorization Code flow with PKCE and receives an ID token whose audience ( aud ) is its own Application (client) ID. GET https://login.microsoftonline.com/{{tenant-id}}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize
 ?client_id={{ConsumerClientId}}
 &response_type=code
 &redirect_uri={{RedirectUri}}
 &scope=openid profile email offline_access
 &state={{State}}&nonce={{Nonce}}
 &code_challenge={{PKCE}}&code_challenge_method=S256 
 2. The API consumer calls the API Management endpoint with the ID token. GET https://{{apim-host}}/{{resource-path}}
Authorization: Bearer {{EntraIdToken}} 
 3. API Management performs the JWT Bearer Token Exchange (RFC 7523) via IAS. After verifying the token, API Management calls the IAS token endpoint. The ID token is the assertion, and the resource parameter targets the IAS dependency that represents the SAP SuccessFactors application. POST https://{{ias-tenant}}.accounts.ondemand.com/oauth2/token
Authorization: Basic base64({{IASClientId}}:{{IASSecret}})
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer
&assertion={{EntraIdToken}}
&resource=urn:sap:identity:application:provider:name:{{dependency}} 
 4. IAS validates the ID token and issues an access token for the employee. IAS selects the corporate identity provider that matches the token's issuer and audience (with Identity Authentication as the application's default identity provider, config step 3) and finds the employee's IAS user by email. The dependency named in resource decides which IAS application the access token is issued for: the IAS application for SAP SuccessFactors. Its Subject Name Identifier sets the token's subject, which identifies the employee in SAP SuccessFactors (config step 4). 
 5. API Management forwards the call to SAP SuccessFactors with the IAS token. GET https://{{sf-api-host}}/odata/v2/{{entity-set}}
Authorization: Bearer {{IASAccessToken}} 
 On the IAS side, the difference from the machine-to-machine pattern lies in flow step 4: which corporate identity provider IAS trusts, whether it resolves the user in its own user store, and what it puts in the subject. 
 Known trade-off: the API consumer sends the employee's Entra ID ID token to API Management as the bearer token. That ID token can now read and write SAP SuccessFactors data as the employee, so treat it as a bearer secret: never log, store or forward it. Microsoft recommends access tokens, not ID tokens, for calling APIs. We used the ID token because its audience is the API consumer's own client ID, which is what IAS checks. The access-token variant is described in Security Considerations. 
 Key Configuration Prerequisites 
 SAP SuccessFactors accepts IAS-issued tokens. Apply part 1 of SAP Note 3681224 . Part 2 (Manage OAuth2 Client Applications) is not needed. 
 An IAS application for SAP SuccessFactors exists, from the standard SAP SuccessFactors and IAS integration. 
 An IAS application for API Management , the application API Management authenticates against, with Grant Type JWT Bearer and a dependency to the SAP SuccessFactors application (in the SAP post: APIM2SF ). 
 User provisioning: each employee exists in Microsoft Entra ID, IAS and SAP SuccessFactors with the same email address, and the IAS user carries the attribute SAP SuccessFactors identifies users by (config step 4). The SAP SuccessFactors to IAS provisioning job (Identity Provisioning) normally maintains the IAS users. 
 Administrator access to the Entra ID app registration of the API consumer (owner or Application Administrator), the IAS administration console and API Management. 
 A REST client such as Postman, to test each step before building the API proxy. 
 Configuration Steps 
 Values in {{double braces}} are placeholders for your own landscape. No secret is ever stored in the API consumer. References read config step N for the numbered sections below, flow step N for the authentication flow above, and test N for the rows of the test table. 
 1. Microsoft Entra ID – App Registration of the API Consumer 
 IAS must trust tokens issued to the API consumer's own app registration . Do not reuse the Entra ID enterprise application configured for SAML single sign-on to IAS or SAP SuccessFactors. 
 Open the app registration the API consumer already signs in with and note its Application (client) ID ( {{ConsumerClientId}} ). Keep the sign-in unchanged: scopes openid profile email , ID tokens from the v2.0 endpoint. 
 Certificates & secrets → New client secret. IAS needs it to configure Entra ID as an OpenID Connect corporate identity provider. Store it only in IAS. If the API consumer is a mobile app or a single-page app, its registration is a public client; the secret and the Web platform are only for IAS, and the app itself never uses them. 
 Authentication → add a platform of type Web with the redirect URI https://{{ias-tenant}}.accounts.ondemand.com/oauth2/callback . It is only needed for the IAS validation check. 
 API permissions → review Microsoft Graph permissions of type Application . Once the app registration has a secret, anyone holding it can use them. Remove those no back end needs. 
 The token sent to API Management is the ID token (see the known trade-off above). A Microsoft Graph access token is rejected by IAS with Invalid JWT ; only Microsoft Graph can validate its own access tokens. 
 2. IAS – Corporate Identity Provider for the API Consumer 
 This was our most important finding. IAS selects the corporate identity provider by the token's issuer and audience. This holds when the application's default identity provider is Identity Authentication (config step 3). An existing Entra ID corporate identity provider used for single sign-on has a different client ID, so IAS rejects the API consumer's token with No trusted corporate IdP found for token issuer . Create a dedicated corporate identity provider. 
 IAS administration console → Identity Providers → Corporate Identity Providers → Create, type OpenID Connect Compliant : 

 Setting 
 Value 

 OpenID Connect Configuration → Discovery URL 
 https://login.microsoftonline.com/{{tenant-id}}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration 

 Client ID 
 {{ConsumerClientId}} 

 Client Secret 
 The secret from config step 1 

 Client Authentication Method 
 Client secret in body 

 Identity Federation → Use Identity Authentication user store 
 On 

 Subject Name Identifier (the Entra ID claim IAS uses to find the IAS user) 
 Email 
 Check: click Load , then save. The provider must show a Last refresh date; without it IAS never loaded the Entra ID signing keys. Also make sure the Client ID has no leading or trailing space. Either mistake makes IAS reject every token, and the message does not point at the cause. 
 Why the user store matters: with the setting off, IAS runs as a pure proxy and passes the Entra ID identity through. The access token then carries the email as its subject plus Entra ID claims such as oid and tid , and in our development tenant SAP SuccessFactors rejected it with Failed to authenticated OIDC token (SAP's exact wording). With the setting on, IAS resolves the employee to an IAS user by email and issues the token for that user, including user_uuid . 
 3. IAS – Application for API Management 
 IAS administration console → Applications & Resources → Applications → the IAS application for API Management: 
 Conditional Authentication: trust the new corporate identity provider, and keep Default Identity Provider = Identity Authentication with no authentication rules. IAS then matches each token to the trusted provider whose client ID equals the token's audience. If a corporate identity provider is the default, IAS checks every token against that provider first. With two providers on the same Entra ID tenant, the other app's tokens fail with JWT aud claim rejected , and we observed the result change from one call to the next. 
 OpenID Connect Configuration → Grant Types: JWT Bearer enabled. 
 Application APIs → Dependencies: a dependency, for example APIM2SF , to the SAP SuccessFactors application. 
 Client Authentication → Secrets: the secret API Management uses. Store it only in an encrypted Key Value Map. 
 Coexistence with the machine-to-machine setup: if you already run the pattern from SAP's post, IAS now has two corporate identity providers on the same Entra ID tenant: one for the service principal and one for the API consumer. That is exactly the case where the default identity provider must stay Identity Authentication. 
 Check: the corporate identity provider's Trusting Applications tab lists the IAS application for API Management. 
 4. IAS – Subject Name Identifiers 
 Two IAS applications take part, and each has its own Subject Name Identifier. In the IAS application for API Management (config step 3), set it to Email : the E

Background 
 The Royal Malaysian Customs Department has issued guidance under Service Tax Policy No. 2/2025 that allows the following invoicing approach for the 2% service tax exemption: 
 Invoicing Method: Rental value with 8% service tax shown, followed by a 2% exemption adjustment, resulting in net 6% service tax charged. 
 For SST-02 reporting purposes: 
 The net taxable service value should be declared under the 6% tax rate in Part C. 
 The service tax collected at 6% (after exemption) should be reported in relevant service tax fields. 
 The 2% exemption amount should be reported in Part D, Field 18(c)(3) – Other Exempted Services 
 Step-by-Step Configuration Guide

 Create a test document with the tax code (e.g., A2). 

 Ensure the transaction posts successfully. 
 b) Run the SST02 report 

 Execute the Malaysia SST-02 return for the test period. 
 Review the output XML or report display. 
 c) Verify the following in the SST02 report: 

 Part C, Tax Box 10: Shows the total service tax collected (at 6% effective rate). 
 Part C, Tax Box 11C_B: Shows the taxable service base amount. 
 Part C, Tax Box 11C_T: Shows the net service tax amount (8% statutory rate - 2% exemption = 6% collected). 
 Part D, Tax Box 18C3: Shows the service value subject to exemption (the base amount on which 2% exemption applies). 
 Expected Result 
 After configuration, your SST-02 report will correctly show: 

 The service value and tax at the effective 6% rate. 
 The 2% exemption reflected in Field 18(c)(3) as required by tax authorities. 
 Key Points to Remember 

 The configuration involves two separate steps : defining tax groups and assigning tax groups to tax boxes. 
 The same tax code (`A2`) is mapped to two different tax groups (`SST_SER_E8` and `SST_SER_E2`). 
 Tax Box `11C_T` has two assignments with different arithmetical operations (one positive, one negative with `-`). 
 The negative operation (`-`) on `SST_SER_E2` in Box `11C_T` performs the exemption calculation 
 No system enhancement is required - standard customizing configuration is sufficient. 
 This configuration follows the Configuring Tax Box Mappings for SST Report as documented in SAP Help Portal. 
 Additional Notes 

 This configuration is based on the guidance from Service Tax Policy No. 2/2025 (Amendment No. 3) for rental and leasing services. 
 The configuration follows SAP's standard DRC (Document and Reporting Compliance) framework 
 Tax group validity dates must match the tax code validity dates. 
 For Malaysia e-Invoice (MyInvoice) alignment, the invoice should clearly show the 8% statutory rate with the 2% exemption deduction. 
 It is recommended to maintain a separate tax code specifically for services subject to this exemption for easier reporting and reconciliation. 
 Always perform thorough testing in your development/test environment before implementing in production. 
 Coordinate with your tax advisors to ensure compliance with all SST02 reporting requirements. 
 Best regards, 
 Lola

items.title: Still struggling with manual monthly invoicing, deductions, and declarations?
items.author: Lola
items.text:
As China's Golden Tax System Phase 4 is implemented and the Fully Digitalized E-Invoice (FDEI) is rolled out nationwide, Value-Added Tax (VAT) is no longer just about a piece of paper—it has become a core compliance mandate that runs through the entire enterprise process of procurement, sales, finance, and tax filing. 
 However, in reality, many companies' invoice management processes are still stuck in a manual mode: "manual download → manual import → spreadsheet reconciliation → printing for declaration." This article provides a systematic overview of the complete SAP S/4HANA Cloud solution for VAT invoice management in China, covering both inbound (input) and outbound (output) VAT. 
 The Real Pain Points for Enterprises 
 Whether for inbound or outbound VAT, corporate tax teams face the following challenges daily: 
 Inbound (Input VAT) Side 
 Lack of transparency in invoice status, leading to frequent cases of lost paper invoices or missed deduction deadlines. 
 Difficulty in linking inbound invoices with SAP business documents, making two-way lookups time-consuming and labor-intensive. 
 Discrepancies between input tax deductions and actual business transactions, resulting in numerous manual adjustments and hidden tax risks. 
 Inability to archive and query Fully Digitalized E-Invoices (FDEI), with a lack of usable inbound VAT reports. 
 Outbound (Output VAT) Side 
 Siloed invoicing and business systems, leading to extensive manual operations and a high risk of errors. 
 Complex requirements for splitting and merging invoices, with a heavy workload for adjusting amount rounding differences. 
 How to issue FDEI in a compliant manner? Can the system keep up with regulatory changes in a timely fashion? 
 SAP provides a complete answer to these challenges. 
 II. Inbound VAT Invoice Management: End-to-End Digitalization from "Receiving" to "Declaring" 
 The inbound invoice management solution in SAP S/4HANA Cloud streamlines the entire process into six clear steps, significantly reducing manual intervention through a direct API connection to the Golden Tax System. 
 Step 1: Automatic Synchronization of Invoice Data The system connects directly to the Golden Tax System via API, automatically pulling inbound invoice data and original files (XML / PDF / OFD) on a scheduled basis, eliminating the need for manual downloads and uploads. For companies that have not yet deployed API integration, the solution also supports batch importing files downloaded from the e-tax platform into S/4HANA, offering flexible compatibility for both modes. 
 Step 2: Mobile Invoice Reception for Purchasers Upon receiving an invoice from a supplier, the purchaser can scan the invoice's QR code with their mobile phone. The system automatically verifies the consistency between the invoice information and the data in SAP. If further action is needed, purchasers must still use the dedicated "Process Inbound VAT Invoices" application to formally receive the invoice. 
 Step 3: Centralized Management and Posting by AP Accountants Accounts Payable (AP) accountants use the "Manage Inbound VAT Invoices" application to view and process all inbound invoices centrally. Each invoice provides a 360° panoramic view, including basic invoice information, associated business documents (supplier invoice, expense report, accounting document), input tax transfer-out records, and its current status in the Golden Tax System—all on a single screen. After verification, the accountant accepts and posts the supplier invoice, achieving financial and tax alignment. 
 Step 4: Direct Connection to Tax Authority for Invoice Verification Through API integration, the system can directly send requests to the State Taxation Administration for FDEI authenticity verification. The verification results (status, time, operator) are automatically written back to the invoice record. This supports batch job scheduling, removing the need for manual, one-by-one verification. In file-based mode, verification results can also be entered manually, flexibly adapting to different companies' integration maturity. 
 Step 5: Month-End Declaration and Input Tax Transfer-Out At the end of each month, the tax accountant processes the monthly declaration in the "Manage Input Tax Declaration" application. The system automatically recommends a list of "declarable" invoices based on criteria such as Golden Tax status, processing status, and whether associated documents have been posted. The declaration can be sent with a single click, and the result is returned from the Golden Tax System and updated automatically. For input tax that needs to be transferred out, the system supports maintaining and posting transfer-out/transfer-in entries with a complete audit trail. In file-based mode, users can batch export a list of declaration-ready invoices from the "Manage Input Tax Declaration" application in a format compatible with the tax authority's template, then upload it to the tax bureau's platform for batch declaration. 
 Step 6: Periodical Statistics Confirmation and Reporting After the monthly declaration is complete, a periodical statistics confirmation request is automatically sent to the Golden Tax System, with its status updated in real-time. The system provides two out-of-the-box operational reports—the Input Tax Deduction Summary and the Input Tax Transfer-Out Summary. These reports can be filtered by company code, business place, and declaration period, and offer both table and chart views to directly assist in filling out VAT declaration supplementary forms. 
 III. Outbound VAT Invoice Management: Business-Driven Invoicing Covering Three Key Scenarios 
 The core concept of the outbound solution is "letting the business system drive invoicing," completely breaking down the data silos between the SD (Sales & Distribution) process, FICA (Financial Contract Accounting) process, Sales Rebates, and the Golden Tax invoicing system. 
 One Solution for Three Main Invoicing Scenarios 
 Blue-Ink Invoice (Standard Invoice): After a sales specialist completes a sales order → delivery → billing document, a finance specialist can directly select the billing document in the DRC (Document and Reporting Compliance) e-invoicing application. The billing information automatically populates the Golden Tax invoice, eliminating repetitive data entry. 
 Red-Ink Invoice (Credit Note): A red-ink reversal request is initiated based on the original blue-ink invoice. After entering the red-ink invoice notification number, the system automatically links the original invoice information for a compliant reversal. 
 Voided Invoice: Invoices can be voided with a single click. In the FDEI scenario, as the tax authority side has no voiding process, the system adapts accordingly. 
 Flexible Invoice Splitting, Merging, and Discount Handling In practice, a single billing document may need to be split into multiple invoices based on an amount threshold, or multiple billing documents may need to be merged into one. SAP supports both standard merging (by line number + tax rate) and special merging (by tax rate only), and allows users to define custom merging dimensions, enabling splitting and invoicing at a granular line-item level. Discount line handling is supported by built-in logic that can automatically capture discount amounts, either merging them into the net amount or displaying them as a separate discount line on the Golden Tax invoice without extra development. 
 Full Support for Fully Digitalized E-Invoices (FDEI) The system supports custom templates from the State Taxation Administration, allowing users to define and update tax authority-required template formats within the system to quickly adapt to regulatory changes. 
 Two Integration Methods for Different Maturity Levels Whether a company has direct connection capabilities or not, SAP has a solution: 
 Direct Connection Mode: Supports three direct connection formats (Aisino, Baiwang, Rongjin—major tax service providers in China) for file-less, automated invoicing. 
 File-Based Mode: Generates an Excel file compatible with the tax authority's format for FDEI. 
 Invoicing Results Automatically Written Back to S/4HANA Information such as invoice number, invoice code, and issued amount is automatically written back to the S/4 billing document, establishing a bi-directional mapping between the billing document and the Golden Tax invoice to ensure data consistency between finance and tax. A new locking mechanism prevents conflicts during concurrent invoicing by multiple users, significantly improving performance in high-volume scenarios. 
 IV. Integration Architecture: SAP DRC + Tax Partners + Golden Tax System 
 SAP employs an open integration architecture, providing universal integration flow templates via the SAP Integration Suite to connect with SAP-certified tax partners (like Rongjin), which in turn communicate with the national Golden Tax System. Companies can also choose to build their own integration interfaces, but they must adhere to the interface standards defined by SAP. This architecture eliminates manual file uploads and downloads, achieving end-to-end automated declaration and archiving. 
 Best regards, 
 Lola

items.title: 每月开票、抵扣、申报，还在靠人力"扛"？ SAP 带你一步迈入增值税发票数字化管理新时代
items.author: Lola
items.text:
随着金税四期落地、全电发票（FDEI）全面推广，增值税已不再只是一张纸的问题——它是贯穿企业采购、销售、财务、税务申报全流程的核心合规命题。 
 然而，现实中许多企业的发票管理依然停留在"人工下载 → 手工导入 → 对表核验 → 打印申报"的模式。本文带你系统了解 SAP S/4HANA Cloud 在中国增值税发票管理上的全套解决方案，覆盖进项与销项两大方向。 
 一、企业面临的真实痛点 
 无论是进项还是销项，企业税务团队每天都要面对以下挑战： 
 进项侧 
 发票状态不透明，纸票丢失、逾期未抵扣的情况时有发生 
 进项发票与 SAP 业务凭证难以关联，双向查询费时费力 
 进项税抵扣与实际业务不符，人工调整多，隐含税务风险 
 全电发票（FDEI）无法归档查询，缺乏可用的进项报表 
 销项侧 
 开票系统与业务系统割裂，大量手工操作，易出错 
 发票拆分、合并需求复杂，金额舍入差异调整工作量大 
 全电发票如何合规开具？法规变化后系统能否及时跟上？ 
 这些问题，SAP 给出了一套完整答案。 
 二、进项增值税发票管理：从" 收票" 到" 申报" 全链路数字化 
 SAP S/4HANA Cloud 的进项发票管理方案，将整个流程压缩为六个清晰步骤，并通过 API 直连金税系统，大幅减少人工干预。 
 第一步：自动同步发票数据 
 系统通过 API 与金税系统直连，按计划任务自动拉取进项发票数据及原始文件（XML / PDF / OFD），无需手动下载上传。对于尚未部署 API 集成的企业，也支持从电税平台下载文件后批量导入 S/4HANA，两种模式灵活兼容。 
 第二步：采购员移动端收票 
 收到供应商发票后，采购员通过手机扫描发票二维码，系统自动比对票面信息与 SAP 数据的一致性。采购人员如果需要进一步处理发票，还是要通过专门的应用"处理增值税进项发票" 去接收发票。 
 第三步：应付会计集中管理与过账 
 应付会计在"管理增值税进项发票"应用中统一查看和处理所有进项发票。每张发票提供 360° 全景视图——发票基本信息、关联的业务凭证（供应商发票、费用报销单、会计凭证）、进项税转出记录，以及在金税系统的当前状态，一屏掌握全貌。完成核验后，会计签收并过账供应商发票，完成财税对齐。 
 第四步：直连税务局完成发票核验 
 通过 API 集成，系统可直接向国家税务局发起全电发票真伪核验请求，核验结果（状态、时间、操作人）自动回写至发票记录，支持批量作业调度，无需人工逐票操作。文件模式下，也可手动录入核验结果，灵活适配不同企业的集成现状。 
 第五步：月末申报与进项税转出 
 每月末，税务会计在"管理进项税申报"应用中处理当月申报。系统根据金税状态、处理状态、关联凭证是否过账等条件，自动推荐"可申报"发票清单。一键发送申报，申报结果由金税系统回传并自动更新。对于需要转出的进项税，系统支持维护并过账转出/转入分录，全程留痕，支持审计。如果是文件模式，用户可以在"管理进项税申报"应用中批量导出符合税局申报模版格式的申报发票列表文件，然后去税局批量上传完成批量申报。 
 第六步：期间统计确认与报表 
 当月申报完成后，期间统计确认请求自动发送至金税系统，状态实时更新。系统提供两张开箱即用的运营报表——进项税抵扣汇总表与进项税转出汇总表，支持按公司代码、业务地点、申报年月筛选，表格与图表双视图，直接辅助增值税申报附表填报。 
 三、销项增值税发票管理：业务驱动开票，三类场景全覆盖 
 销项方案的核心理念是"让业务系统驱动开票"，彻底打通 SD 流程，FICA流程，Sales Rebate与金税开票之间的数据隔阂。 
 三类发票场景，一套方案全覆盖 
 蓝票（正常开票） ：销售专员完成销售订单→交货→账单后，财务专员直接在 DRC 金税开票应用中拾取账单，账单信息自动填入金税发票，无需重复录入。 
 红票（冲销开票） ：凭原蓝票发起红冲申请，输入红字通知号，系统自动关联原始发票信息，合规冲销。 
 废票（废票处理） ：选择发票一键作废；全电发票场景下，税务局侧无废票流程，系统相应适配处理。 
 灵活的拆票、合票与折扣处理 
 实际业务中，一张账单可能需要按金额上限拆分为多张发票，或将多张账单合并开具。SAP 支持普通合并（按行号+税率）与特殊合并（仅按税率），并允许用户自定义合并维度，精细到行项目级别的拆分开票。折扣行处理支持内置逻辑，可自动取抓折扣金额，净额合并或作为折扣行显示于金税发票，无需额外开发。 
 全电发票（FDEI ）全面支持 
 系统支持国税局自定义模板，用户可在系统内定义并随时更新税务局要求的模板格式，快速适配法规变化。 
 两种对接方式，满足不同集成成熟度 
 无论企业当前是否具备直连能力，SAP 均有方案： 
 直连模式 ：航信，百旺，容津三种直连格式，实现无文件化自动开票 
 文件模式 ：生成国税局的EXCEL （数电票） 
 开票结果自动回写 S/4HANA 
 发票号、发票代码、开票金额等信息自动回写至 S/4 账单，建立账单与金税发票的双向映射关系，实现财税数据一致性。新锁定机制支持多人并发开票不互锁，大批量场景下性能显著提升。 
 四、集成架构：SAP DRC + 税务合作伙伴 + 金税系统 
 SAP 采用开放的集成架构，通过 SAP Integration Suite 提供通用集成流模板，对接经 SAP 认证的税务合作伙伴（如容津等），最终与国家金税系统完成通信。企业也可选择自建集成接口，但需遵循 SAP 定义的接口标准。整个架构消除了文件上传下载的手工操作，实现端到端的自动化申报与归档。 
 五、核心价值总结 

 维度 
 传统模式 
 SAP DRC 方案 

 数据同步 
 手工下载/导入 
 API 自动定时同步 

 发票核验 
 逐票人工核对 
 批量自动核验，结果自动回写 

 月末申报 
 手动整理清单，逐步操作 
 系统推荐清单，一键申报 

 开票效率 
 业务/开票两套系统，重复录入 
 业务驱动，数据自动带入 

 拆合票处理 
 人工拆分，舍入差手工调整 
 内置规则，支持行项目级操作 

 全电发票 
 无归档查询，难以适配 
 全面支持 FDEI 格式与归档 

 合规可审计 
 状态不透明，操作难追溯 
 全生命周期状态留痕，完整审计链 
 Best regards, 
 Lola

items.title: Resolving "A technical error has occurred while reading the time data" in Employee Central Time Off
items.author: Gayathri_V26
items.text:
Introduction 
 In an integration between SuccessFactors Employee Central (EC) Time Off and SAP ERP HCM, time data is replicated from EC to the ERP system. After this replication, the following error while reading time data: 
 A technical error has occurred while reading the time data. See long text. 
 This post describes the root cause I found and how I resolved it with the standard clean-up report. 
 Problem 
 While reading the replicated time data, the system raised the error above, and the long text gave no clear indication of the cause. 
 Analysis 
 I compared the two tables that hold the replicated data: 
 PA2010: Employee Remuneration Info (Infotype 2010) 
 PAOCFEC_REFMAP: the mapping table between EC time records (external code) and the ERP infotype records 
 The record counts did not match. Some PA2010 entries had no mapping entry in PAOCFEC_REFMAP, and some PAOCFEC_REFMAP entries had no matching record in PA2010. This inconsistency causes the technical error when the time data is read. 
 Solution 
 SAP provides a standard clean-up report for this: 
 Report: ECTIM_CLEANUP_REFMAP_INFTY_TAB 
 Description: Clean-Up of Employee Time Data Replicated from Employee Central 
 Steps: 
 Go to transaction SA38 and run ECTIM_CLEANUP_REFMAP_INFTY_TAB. 
 Keep Test Mode selected for the first run. 
 Under Run Modes: 
 Enter the date in Clean Up Data As Of (in my case, 01.05.2025). 
 Select Delete Inconsistent Entries. Use Delete All Entries only if you really want to remove everything. 
 Under Infotype Selection, choose Infotype 2010 (or 2001, depending on your scenario). 
 Under Additional Criteria for Deleting Inconsistent Entries, you can restrict the run by Personnel Number, Absence Type or Wage Type. I restricted it to the affected employee. 
 Execute the report in test mode and review the result. 
 Test mode result 
 The test run lists exactly which entries are inconsistent: 

 Entries missing in PAOCFEC_REFMAP: these records will be deleted from PA2010. The output shows PERNR, SUBTY, BEGDA, ENDDA and SEQNR. 
 Entries missing in PA2010: these records will be deleted from PAOCFEC_REFMAP. The output shows PERNR and EXTERNALCODE. 
 This matched the mismatch I found when comparing the tables. 
 Live run 
 After confirming the test result, I ran the report again with Test Mode unchecked, using the same selection. The report deleted the inconsistent entries. 
 Result 
 After the live run, the tables were consistent again. The time data could be read without errors, and the issue was resolved. 
 Key takeaways 
 If you get this error, compare PA2010 (or PA2001) with PAOCFEC_REFMAP. 
 Always run ECTIM_CLEANUP_REFMAP_INFTY_TAB in test mode first and check what will be deleted. 
 Use the personnel number, absence type or wage type restrictions to limit the clean-up to the affected employees. 
 Run the live clean-up in a development or quality system first, or get approval before running it in production, because the report deletes data. 
 After clean-up, re-replicate the affected time records from Employee Central if they are still needed. 

 Conclusion 
 Inconsistencies between the ERP time infotype tables and the EC reference mapping table can cause the "technical error while reading the time data". The standard report ECTIM_CLEANUP_REFMAP_INFTY_TAB finds and removes these inconsistencies. I hope this helps anyone facing the same issue. Feel free to share your experience in the comments.
