items.text:
Hello, 
 we export manual test cases from SAP Cloud ALM into Excel, CSV and HTML, using the Test Cases API ( calm-testmanagement/v1 : ManualTestCases → Activities → Actions). The export works well for the test case definitions. 
 Our customer now also needs the results of manual test runs per action (test step) in the same export: 
 action status set by the tester (e.g. passed / failed) 
 execution date 
 name of the tester who executed the step 
 the tester's notes or actual result for the step 
 These values are visible in the Test Execution app, but we could not find them in any public API: 
 Test Cases API: only the test case definitions. The bound action forceDeletionIncludingTestRunsAndResults shows that test runs and results exist, but they cannot be read. 
 Test Plans API: test plans, assigned test cases and the assigned tester ( testerId ), but no runs or results. 
 Test Execution Analytics API ( DP_TESTS 😞 status per test case from a daily snapshot, and action counts ( passedActions , FailedActions , …), but no action-level dimension, so we cannot see which step passed or failed. 
 Test Automation API: for automated tests only. 
 My questions: 
 Is there currently any API (or another supported way) to read manual test run results at action level, including status, execution date, tester and notes? 
 If not: is such an API planned? If yes, is there a roadmap item we can follow? 
 Is there a recommended workaround for an automated export of step-level results?

110.summary: A detailed troubleshooting post about SAP Cloud Transport Management (CTMS) export of Cloud Integration content failing in every case. Both the CPI Transport button and the Content Agent download fail with CREATE_MTAR_CONTENT_ERROR and an S3 PUT rejection, including for SAP Destination Service content. The poster checked destinations, role and token scopes, and recreated the instance and key, which points to Content Agent's internal storage upload rather than the CPI configuration. The post asks three questions and contains no answer.
key_points: Both export paths fail: CPI Transport (MTAR export) and Content Agent UI download.
Error on the CPI path is HTTP 500 from POST /api/1.0/transportcontents with CREATE_MTAR_CONTENT_ERROR.
Download path fails at 'Server rejected operation connecting to PUT ... s3 ...' after the export process starts and initialises.
Failure also happens for destination content, which is not Cloud Integration, so the cause is probably not in the CPI setup.
The poster asks whether the free Integration Suite plan or subaccount settings could block the S3 upload.
technical_details: SAP Cloud Transport Management (CTMS), standard instance, landscape Dev to Prod.
Content Agent Service, standard instance with free (Application) subscription.
Destinations: ContentAssemblyService, CloudIntegration, TransportManagementService.
BTP region Singapore (AWS, ap11); SAP Integration Suite free plan (Cloud Integration).
Process Integration Runtime (api plan) with roles WorkspacePackagesTransport, WorkspacePackagesRead, WorkspacePackagesEdit.
Error text: CREATE_MTAR_CONTENT_ERROR; 'Export Operation has failed. Retry the export process.'; S3 PUT to an hcp-xxxx.s3-ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com path.
110.why_it_matters: It is a well-documented isolation exercise: by showing the failure is independent of content type and CPI credentials, it narrows the search to the Content Agent side. It is useful for anyone setting up CTMS transport for Cloud Integration on a free or trial-like plan.
110.developer_problem: Content Agent exports for CTMS fail for every content type with an S3 PUT rejection, and the poster needs to know whether it is a plan restriction or a subaccount-side problem.
110.teaching_angle: Strong case study for teaching systematic isolation in BTP: list what was varied (content type, credentials, destinations, instance recreation) and what remained constant (region, plan, S3 upload). Ask trainees to propose the next checks, such as the subscription entitlements, the Content Agent service key, and the BTP support component for the region. Note that the thread has no confirmed cause.

digest.headline: A light day for core ABAP: FOR ALL ENTRIES versus CTEs, a CDS-versus-SE16N stale data claim, AL11 background file failures, plus Joule A2A migration and principal propagation posts.
digest.overview:
Most of today's material is truncated blog intros and unanswered forum questions. The usable ABAP content is a discussion on FOR ALL ENTRIES versus CTEs, joins and internal tables as SQL sources (ref 47), a claim that custom CDS views over simplified tables return stale data compared with SE16N (ref 3), and two duplicate questions about OPEN DATASET working in foreground but not in background (refs 17, 20). A CJ20N BAdI question (ref 48) is a good LUW and enqueue case.

On the BTP side, the Joule A2A migration post (ref 23) gives a concrete map from Customer-Managed Joule to SAP-managed Joule. Principal propagation appears in several posts: SuccessFactors via Entra ID and APIM (ref 68), an MCP server to S/4 (ref 78), and a Work Zone card (ref 80). Many items are excerpts only, so their claims, especially ref 3, need checking before you repeat them.

top_stories.title: FOR ALL ENTRIES vs CTEs, joins and internal tables as SQL sources
top_stories.summary: A discussion covers the empty-driver-table trap, where an initial driver table makes FAE read without the restriction, and the duplicate removal FAE performs. It shows alternatives: WITH +cte, an inner join, and SELECT FROM @itab (7.52+). It also notes that large internal tables passed to Open SQL can cause memory spikes, and that joins and FAE are not always semantically identical. Claims like FAE being obsolete in ABAP Cloud and the 5,000–10,000 batch size are unsourced.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It is a direct code-review topic for S/4HANA. The empty-driver guard and pushing logic into one database roundtrip are habits your trainees should have. Measure with ST05 or SQL Monitor rather than trusting the unsourced figures.

top_stories.title: CDS view vs SE16N returning different data for simplified tables
top_stories.summary: The post claims a custom CDS view over simplified ECC tables (MBEWH, ANEK, ANEP) returns stale data, while SE16N returns live S/4HANA figures. It attributes this to CDS bypassing table redirection and proposes ST05 plans as proof. The excerpt ends before any evidence.
top_stories.why_it_matters: If it is true, it changes which objects you should read in S/4HANA. Treat it as unproven until you reproduce it and check the compatibility views and redirection status of the target tables.

top_stories.title: AL11 file written in foreground but not in background
top_stories.summary: Two duplicate questions report that a report using OPEN DATASET, TRANSFER and CLOSE DATASET creates the CSV in foreground but not as a background job under a batch user. No code, sy-subrc values or job log are given. The likely areas to check are S_DATASET authorization, the path, and which application server runs the job. These are not confirmed in the posts.
top_stories.why_it_matters: Silent file failures are common in production. The usual cause is that sy-subrc after OPEN DATASET is never checked.

top_stories.title: Joule A2A: migrating BTP code-based agents to SAP-managed Joule
top_stories.summary: The post lays out three paths for custom agents connected to Customer-Managed Joule: Joule Studio 2.0, outbound A2A to Joule Work (roadmap, not yet available), and Markdown Joule skills. Capability YAMLs can be imported as a short-term bridge. Joule Studio 2.0 agents are Python and LangChain-pattern A2A agents on a managed runtime. The runtime handles IAS registration, and only APIs where principal propagation can be enforced are reachable. Third-party MCP is on the roadmap.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It states the constraints (PP-only APIs, no outbound A2A yet) that decide whether migration is viable now.

top_stories.title: Principal propagation for agents and apps: SuccessFactors, MCP, Work Zone
top_stories.summary: The SuccessFactors post uses Entra ID login, an APIM JWT bearer exchange (RFC 7523) at IAS, and SAP Note 3681224 part 1. It flags using the ID token as the bearer as a trade-off. Ref 78 is an intro only, on IAS authentication and XSUAA authorization from an MCP server to S/4HANA Cloud. Ref 80 asks why an OAuth2SAMLBearerAssertion destination returns an IAS login page in a Work Zone UI Integration Card.
top_stories.why_it_matters: Technical users in agent and app integrations weaken auditing. The token chain is where these setups usually break.

top_stories.title: CJ20N: copying project dates to the Level-1 CAPEX WBS
top_stories.summary: The author cannot call BAPIs synchronously in the save BAdI because of enqueue locks, and found no PRTE row exists for a new WBS until the Dates tab is opened. They propose writing directly to PRTE with FLGVM = 'X' from PROJECTDEF_UPDATE~AT_SAVE, and ask about an asynchronous BAPI call as an alternative.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It is a good case on BAdI choice, LUW and locks. A direct write to a standard scheduling table is a risk, and the PRTE behaviour claims need verification.

top_stories.title: EC Time Off error fixed with ECTIM_CLEANUP_REFMAP_INFTY_TAB
top_stories.summary: The fix for 'A technical error has occurred while reading the time data' is to compare PA2010 or PA2001 with PAOCFEC_REFMAP, then run the standard report in test mode, followed by a live run restricted by selection and set to Delete Inconsistent Entries.
top_stories.why_it_matters: It is a supported fix with no manual table edits. The post cites no SAP Note and does not explain how the inconsistency arose.

top_stories.title: Content Agent export to CTMS fails with CREATE_MTAR_CONTENT_ERROR
top_stories.summary: Exports fail for every content type with an S3 PUT rejection, including destination content. Credentials, roles and instance recreation did not help. This points at the Content Agent storage upload, not CPI. There is no answer yet.
top_stories.why_it_matters: The isolation approach is instructive, but no cause is confirmed.

deep_dives.title: FOR ALL ENTRIES vs CTE, join and internal-table SQL source
deep_dives.explanation:
`FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_vbak` has two well-known hazards. If the driver table is initial, the restriction is dropped and the statement reads without the corresponding condition, so you need an `IF lt_vbak IS NOT INITIAL` guard. It also removes duplicate rows from the result set, which costs extra processing and can change the result if you expected duplicates.

The alternatives in the discussion are a CTE with `WITH +open_orders AS ( ... ) SELECT ... INNER JOIN vbap`, a plain join when both sides are in the database, and `SELECT ... FROM @lt_vbak AS o INNER JOIN vbap` (7.52+), which uses an internal table as a data source. The CTE and join push the work into a single database roundtrip. The internal-table source still ships the table to the database, so large tables can cause memory pressure, as the post notes.

The post says joins and FAE are not semantically identical when the driver set comes from separate logic. An inner join with an internal table does not deduplicate the way FAE does, so you may need DISTINCT or a prepared driver table. Claims in the post such as FAE being obsolete in ABAP Cloud and a 5,000–10,000 batch size have no source and should not be taught as fact. Measure with ST05 or SQL Monitor.
key_concepts: Internal table as SQL data source (7.52+)

deep_dives.title: Debugging OPEN DATASET failures in background jobs
deep_dives.explanation:
Two posts describe a CSV written with `OPEN DATASET`, `TRANSFER` and `CLOSE DATASET` that appears in AL11 when run in foreground and does not appear in a background job under a batch user. Neither shows code or a sy-subrc value. The post text does not give a cause. The areas worth checking are general ABAP knowledge, not from the posts.

First, check `sy-subrc` after `OPEN DATASET`, and use the `MESSAGE msg` addition to capture the OS message. Write path, sy-subrc and message to the job log. Second, the batch user needs authorization object `S_DATASET` for the path and activity. Third, the job may run on a different application server than the one where you looked in AL11, so check the target server in SM37. Fourth, use logical file names (FILE, `FILE_GET_NAME`) instead of hard-coded physical paths, so the path resolves per system.

The lesson for trainees is that file I/O must report failure explicitly. Without checks, a failed open looks like a successful run.

deep_dives.title: CDS view vs SE16N on simplified tables: how to test the claim
deep_dives.explanation:
The post claims a custom CDS view over simplified ECC tables (MBEWH, ANEK, ANEP) returns stale data, while SE16N shows live S/4HANA figures, and that CDS bypasses table redirection. The excerpt has no evidence, so treat it as a hypothesis to test.

A sandbox test: select from the table in SE16N and in a custom CDS view, then run both with an ST05 SQL trace and compare the statements and plans. Check what object each actually reads. Check whether the target tables are replaced by compatibility views or redirection, and whether the data is expected to exist in the old table at all in S/4HANA. Identify which result is correct before concluding anything about redirection.

The practical rule that comes out regardless is to read released CDS views or the new data model objects for a simplified area rather than the legacy table, and verify against the simplification documentation.

post_drafts.title: FAE empty driver trap
post_drafts.text:
*FOR ALL ENTRIES: the classic trap*

If the driver table is empty, FAE reads without the restriction from it.

*Always guard:*
IF lt_vbak IS NOT INITIAL.
  SELECT ... FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_vbak ...
ENDIF.

Also, FAE removes duplicate rows from the result.

Alternatives on 7.52+: a CTE with WITH +name, a join, or SELECT ... FROM @lt_vbak AS o INNER JOIN vbap.

*Measure with ST05 or SQL Monitor before switching.*

https://community.sap.com/t5/abap-forum/beyond-for-all-entries-are-you-still-using-it-on-s-4hana-or-have-ctes-amp/m-p/14528315#M1506

post_drafts.title: File works in foreground, not in background?
post_drafts.text:
*OPEN DATASET works in foreground but not in a background job?*

Don't guess. Check:
1. sy-subrc after OPEN DATASET (use the MESSAGE addition)
2. S_DATASET authorization for the batch user
3. Which app server the job ran on (SM37)
4. Use logical file names, not hard-coded paths

Write the result to the job log. Never let a file write fail silently.

https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-q-a/application-server-al11-file-not-uploaded-using-background-job/qaq-p/14527812

interview_questions.question: A report uses FOR ALL ENTRIES and sometimes returns far too many rows in production. What is the likely cause, and how would you fix and modernize the code?
interview_questions.answer: The likely cause is an empty driver table. With FOR ALL ENTRIES, an initial driver table causes the read to happen without the restriction that depends on it, so it can return a large result. The fix is an IF driver IS NOT INITIAL guard. FAE also removes duplicate rows from the result, which adds overhead and can change semantics. To modernize, use a join or CTE (WITH +name) when the data is in the database, or SELECT FROM @itab AS alias INNER JOIN on 7.52+ when the driver is an internal table. Be careful that a join does not deduplicate like FAE, so you may need DISTINCT. Large internal tables passed to Open SQL can cause memory pressure, so I would verify with ST05 or SQL Monitor.

interview_questions.question: A program writes a CSV with OPEN DATASET in foreground but no file appears when scheduled as a background job. How do you diagnose it?
interview_questions.answer: First make the failure visible: check sy-subrc after OPEN DATASET, TRANSFER and CLOSE DATASET, use the MESSAGE addition to get the OS text, and write path, sy-subrc and message to the job log. Then compare the contexts. The batch user needs S_DATASET authorization for the path. The job may run on a different application server than the one I inspected in AL11, so I check the target server in SM37. The OS-level permission of the directory for the SAP system user matters too. For production I would use logical file names via FILE and FILE_GET_NAME instead of physical paths, so the path resolves per system. The posts themselves give no cause, so these are checks, not conclusions.

interview_questions.question: In a CJ20N save BAdI, BAPI calls fail because of enqueue locks. A colleague proposes writing directly to PRTE. How would you evaluate that?
interview_questions.answer: A direct write to PRTE bypasses SAP's consistency logic for scheduling data, so I would treat it as high risk and not accept it without evidence that it is supported. The BAPIs fail in the save BAdI because the project objects are locked by the same transaction, and the save LUW is not finished. I would look for a supported route inside the project update logic, such as changing the data structures the BAdI exposes, or a call that runs after the LUW commits, for example an asynchronous or update-task call that runs once the locks are released. I would also check the BAdI choice: the author notes WORKBREAKDOWN_UPDATE~AT_SAVE gets an empty IT_WBS_ELEMENT when only header dates change. Any approach needs testing for locking and rollback behaviour, and the claim that PRTE rows are not created for new WBS elements should be verified.
